source_text.Q-1042: MEDIUM, owner CI lane (follow-up of Q-1037, the next lever after sharding). Reported by the supervisor 2026-10-08. Evidence: ExUnit reports ~0.5 s average per test and ~66 min of cumulative test work per backend run (7.7k tests); a large share is believed to be the per-test tenant schema clone from tenant_template (CREATE SCHEMA ... LIKE tenant_template... for every table, see the LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE setup/teardown log lines and the 'tenant_template_build' schemas): cost per test = DDL for every table of the template plus DROP SCHEMA CASCADE at teardown. NOT yet measured: step 1 is to instrument (time per clone, number of tables cloned, share of test time) on one partition, step 2 choose the lever: (a) clone only the tables the test needs, (b) share a read-only tenant across tests that do not mutate it (async-safe), (c) a pooled tenant per module with truncate-reset, (d) Postgres schema cloning via CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE or a faster mechanism; keep isolation guarantees (no cross-test leakage, the ISS-0410-class isolation bugs). Each step measured before/after; mutation proof that isolation still holds (a test that leaves data behind must not leak into the next). Overlap check 2026-10-08: Q-1037 is the umbrella; ISS-0410 (isolation failure, blocked) is background, not a duplicate.

WF-03 Step 3 / WF-02 Step 2d: IDIOM REVIEW (hard gate) for ISS-1042 / Q-1042. Role file .claude/agents/reviewer.md: idiomatic OTP vs crutch, supervision integrity, type-safety gaps, scope creep, consistency with docs/migration/decisions/. Also docs/anti-patterns.md.

Implementer handoff: handoffs/WF03-ISS1042-20261012/step-03-elixir-dev.json (deviations are listed in result.issues). Security gate: PASS out-of-scope (handoffs/WF03-ISS1042-20261012/step-03c-security-reviewer.json). Spec: lib/letflow/design/iss1042-pooled-tenant-fixture.md.

SPECIFIC QUESTIONS you must answer with evidence:
1. The pool worker is started with GenServer.start (UNLINKED, not under any supervisor) so it outlives setup_all until the module's on_exit. Is that an idiomatic-OTP crutch? What happens if the owning module's process crashes or on_exit never runs (ExUnit abort, --max-failures, timeout kill): does the worker, its schema, and its Postgres connection leak, and is there a reaper/monitor? Would ExUnit.Callbacks.start_supervised!/start_link_supervised! (ExUnit's test-supervisor) or a monitor on the owner pid be correct instead? Verdict: acceptable with the stated mitigation, or FAIL with the exact fix.
2. Hidden global state: any named process, ETS table, persistent_term, Application env, or process-dictionary keys introduced; is each cleaned up on every exit path; can two modules in the same BEAM (async: false modules run serially, but async modules run concurrently with a pooled module) interfere?
3. Scope creep: the implementer added API beyond the design (parity_check opt, generations map in pool_stats, optional reset args). Are they used (by the adopted modules or by the stated TEST-DESIGNER need) or dead? Is 1306 added lines in tenant_fixture.ex proportionate, any duplicated logic with tenant_template.ex, and does the default (non-pool) path remain unchanged? Quote the single dispatch point.
4. Error handling: any bare rescue/catch-all that swallows errors, `{:ok, _} =` matches on fallible paths, timeouts of :infinity without a guard against a hung worker blocking the whole test run (a hung pool worker must fail the module loudly within a bounded time, not stall CI for the 30 min watchdog). Judge, with the code.
5. Decision-record consistency: nothing contradicts docs/migration/decisions/ (esp. the ISS-0113/0410 isolation lineage, REQ-045 no per-instance supervised process).
6. The security reviewer's optional F2 (assert current_database() matches the test database in start_pool!/2): recommend ADOPT or SKIP with a reason; if ADOPT, say whether it is a blocker (then FAIL) or a follow-up.
7. Documentation: the anti-patterns entry and ISS-1042.yaml measurements are accurate against the handoff's numbers (spot-check 3 figures).
FAIL on a genuine crutch, broken supervision/lifecycle that leaks resources or can hang CI, or scope creep; otherwise PASS with non-blocking notes recorded. Read-only: do not modify files other than your handoff. Complete the handoff per docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, commit and push. Do not edit handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log.

result.summary: PASS with non-blocking notes. Reviewed git diff origin/main...HEAD (test/, docs/anti-patterns.md, docs/issues/ISS-1042.yaml; no lib/ code change). Q1 unlinked GenServer.start: ACCEPTABLE, not a crutch. start_supervised!/start_link_supervised! would be WRONG here: ExUnit's OnExitHandler terminates the test supervisor BEFORE running on_exit callbacks, so a supervised worker would already be dead when pool_teardown! needs it to DROP the schemas; a link has the same defect (stated in the Pool moduledoc). Registration order is correct: on_exit(pool_teardown!) is registered immediately after GenServer.start and before the create_slots call, so a failing slot clone is still torn down. Exit paths: module-process crash, setup_all timeout and --max-failures still run the module on_exit (ExUnit runs it from the runner after the module process ends); if the worker is already dead pool_teardown! logs a warning and TenantSchemaReaper sweeps the schemas (same posture as the pre-existing per-test fixture). A hard VM kill (CI watchdog) takes worker and connections with it. No monitor/reaper is needed and none recommended; a named process left behind only makes a later start_pool! for the SAME module raise already_started, loudly. Q2 hidden global state: one registered name per module (Module.concat(Letflow.TenantFixture.Pool, module)), released on GenServer.stop or VM exit; process-dictionary keys (@pool_key/@claims_key/@fence_key) live in the per-test process only; NO ETS, persistent_term, Application env or Process.register added (the only persistent_term in the area is TenantTemplate's pre-existing @built_marker_key). Interference: pooled modules are rejected unless async: false, ExUnit runs sync modules after async ones and serially, each partition has its own database, and names are per module, so no concurrent pooled module and no collision. Q3 scope: the single dispatch point is `case pool_dispatch(opts) do {:pooled, fixture} -> fixture; :default -> default_provisioned_tenant!(opts) end` at tenant_fixture.ex ~241-252, directly after the unchanged Sandbox.mode(:auto) line; the only removed line in the file diff is a typespec line, the original body moved verbatim into default_provisioned_tenant!/1. Extra API: `extra:` opt is used (reset_public! at fixture ~1770); recycle_pool!/pool_dirty_report/pool_stats are exercised by tenant_fixture_dispatch_test; parity_check:, pool_end_fence!/0 and pool_stats.generations have no caller yet and exist for TEST-DESIGNER step 4 (stated need) - non-blocking, see R2. Size: ~887 added pool lines in tenant_fixture.ex plus 589 in tenant_template.ex for a validated 14-section design (definitional digest, fences, rebuild) is proportionate; no behaviour/macro/framework abstraction introduced; ident/literal helpers are re-implemented privately in the Pool next to tenant_template's quote helpers - tiny duplication, watch item. Q4 error handling: no swallowing catch-alls. Every worker handle_call rescue converts the exception to {:error, message} that the client raises as ExUnit.AssertionError (fail-closed, message preserved); `throw {:pool_fail, ...}` is internal control flow caught in the same handle_call; teardown collects per-step errors and reports them. Two bare rescues in owning_module/0 and test_process?/0 introspect ExUnit process dictionaries and degrade to nil/false (see R3). No `{:ok, _} =` matches on fallible paths (call results are case-matched). Timeouts: call_worker! uses :infinity (design M4) but the worker is bounded: resets run under SET LOCAL lock_timeout 3s / statement_timeout 30s (tenant_template.ex:295-296), fences have fixed 250/500 ms budgets, other Repo queries carry the DBConnection default 15 s, so the worker replies or errors; and test_helper sets no ExUnit :timeout override (ExUnit.start(exclude: ...)), so ExUnit's default 60 s per test/setup_all/on_exit kills a client blocked on a truly hung worker and fails the module loudly, long before the 30 min watchdog. Acceptable. Q5 decisions: nothing contradicts docs/migration/decisions (0009 pool sizing untouched; fixture stays test-only; Sandbox.mode(:auto) contract of ISS-0113/0423 preserved and set first in start_pool!/pool_teardown!/run_end_fence!; REQ-045 untouched - the module-scoped worker is test infrastructure, not an engine instance process, InstanceSupervisor not involved; ISS-0410 lineage addressed by public keyed-row counts and tenants/tenant_schemas snapshot compare). Q6 F2 (assert current_database()): ADOPT as a non-blocking follow-up (R1), not a blocker: start_pool! issues TRUNCATE/DROP SCHEMA CASCADE/DELETE on public, the pre-existing teardown already does DROP SCHEMA CASCADE under the same structural protection (elixirc_paths + config/test.exs letflow_test<partition>); the check is one cheap query. Q7 docs: spot-checks against the step-03 handoff match: identity_id_hardening 95.2 s -> 14.4 s (81 clean/30 reset/2 rebuilt), definitions/store_test 37.3 s -> 50.3 s (buggy digest) -> 10.3 s, digest 905 definition rows at 15-16 ms alone / 19-26 ms full probe. One wording inaccuracy (R4). ISS-1042 acceptance criterion 2 (5+5 runs) stays open by design for TEST-RUNNER. I did not run mix test (read-only review); behavioural evidence is the implementer's quoted 247-pass run, extended by TEST-DESIGNER M1..M22.

issues.description: Follow-up: adopt security F2 - assert current_database() starts with letflow_test (the configured test database) in start_pool!/2 or Pool.init before any DDL. Non-blocking.
parity_check: opt, pool_end_fence!/0 and pool_stats.generations have no caller outside the pool code yet; keep only if TEST-DESIGNER consumes them at step 4, otherwise remove (scope creep).

owning_module/0 and test_process?/0 rescue-all to nil/false: a future ExUnit internals change would silently disable the misordered-attach rejection (falls back to per-test clone, slower not unsafe). TEST-DESIGNER should include a test that the rejection still fires.

Docs: docs/anti-patterns.md item 2 and ISS-1042.yaml server_side_microbenchmarks say TRUNCATE of "all 57 tables of a clone"; a clone has 50 plain tables, 57 is the template incl. partitions. Correct at DOC-UPDATER step.

Type-safety observation (does not block): worker state, slot records and the process-dictionary claim map are untyped plain maps with atom statuses; a @type or small struct for slot/state would make a missing :baseline or invalid status unrepresentable rather than caught by probes/tests. Role file says to file this under docs/issues tagged type-safety; NOT filed by me because this dispatch limits REVIEWER to editing only its own handoff - ORCH please file it (low priority, test infrastructure).

Implementer deviations from design 3.2/3.4 (unlinked start, tenant_snapshot not re-taken on rebuild, FK graph recomputed per reset) judged sound; design text should be updated by CODE-DESIGNER/DOC-UPDATER if the doc is kept.
